name: EXP_045 v9.10 qualitative figure codebook
revision_note: Frozen six-axis codebook tree for claim-level backfill. This file is not an automated atom remap; claim counts are pending direct backfill.

children.name: Image Appearance
children.definition: Whole-panel, crop-level, or panel-level low-level visual appearance.
children.evaluator_question: Does the figure, crop, or panel have acceptable low-level visual appearance?
children.positive_scope: Blur, noise, exposure, contrast, color, lighting, global artifact, realism, and style.
children.negative_scope: Object shape errors, spatial relation errors, prompt mismatch, reference mismatch, point distribution, keypoint accuracy, mask accuracy, and latent attention-map behavior.

children.name: Blur
children.definition: Focus loss, smear, or blur visible at the panel or crop level.

children.name: Noise
children.definition: Random speckle, grain, sensor-like corruption, or noisy visual artifacts.

children.name: Exposure
children.definition: Over-exposure, under-exposure, saturation clipping, or visibility loss from brightness.

children.name: Contrast
children.definition: Insufficient or excessive tonal separation that harms visible interpretation.

children.name: Color
children.definition: Color cast, color inconsistency, or visually implausible color independent of prompt/reference criteria.

children.name: Lighting
children.definition: Illumination, shadow, reflection, or lighting quality visible in the output.

children.name: Global Artifact
children.definition: Panel-wide artifact not better explained by object form, layout, relation, prompt, or reference match.

children.name: Realism
children.definition: Overall perceptual plausibility or photorealism when not tied to a specific object, prompt, or reference.

children.name: Style
children.definition: Global visual style or aesthetic quality when judged directly rather than as reference or prompt match.

children.name: Object Form
children.definition: Internal quality of visible objects, regions, bodies, faces, surfaces, and masks.
children.evaluator_question: Are visible objects or regions internally well-formed?
children.positive_scope: Shape, boundary, texture, surface, material, completeness, pose, face, anatomy, detail, and segmentation boundary quality.
children.negative_scope: Whole-scene arrangement, pairwise relation, explicit prompt matching, and visible reference or ground-truth matching.

children.name: Shape
children.definition: Object geometry, silhouette, deformation, or structural shape correctness.

children.name: Boundary
children.definition: Object or region edge quality, contour sharpness, silhouette completeness, or boundary artifacts.

children.name: Texture
children.definition: Local texture quality, texture continuity, or texture corruption on visible regions.

children.name: Surface
children.definition: Surface smoothness, topology, wrinkles, holes, or visible surface defects.

children.name: Material
children.definition: Material appearance or material property quality of an object or region.

children.name: Completeness
children.definition: Missing, truncated, duplicated, or incomplete object parts.

children.name: Pose
children.definition: Pose plausibility of a single visible object, body, or articulated entity when not judged against ground truth.

children.name: Face
children.definition: Face-specific form quality including expression quality when not prompt- or reference-driven.

children.name: Anatomy
children.definition: Body, limb, hand, joint, or anatomical plausibility of one entity.

children.name: Detail
children.definition: Fine detail, thin structures, small parts, or local feature preservation.

children.name: Segmentation
children.definition: Mask or segmentation visual quality when judged as object-region form rather than GT match.

children.name: Scene Layout
children.definition: Scene-level spatial organization and physical arrangement.
children.positive_scope: Composition, depth, scale, view, spatial distribution, occlusion layout, camera geometry, and physical plausibility.
children.negative_scope: Object-internal defects, exact pairwise relation claims, explicit reference matching, and prompt-specific layout instructions.

children.name: Composition
children.definition: Overall arrangement of regions, objects, foreground, background, or panel contents.

children.name: Depth
children.definition: Depth ordering, 3D arrangement, or perceived scene depth.

children.name: Scale
children.definition: Relative or absolute size plausibility at scene level.

children.name: View
children.definition: Viewpoint, novel-view layout, or multi-view scene-level consistency.

children.name: Spatial Distribution
children.definition: Distribution, spacing, clumping, or spread of visible scene elements or point samples.

children.name: Occlusion Layout
children.definition: Occlusion ordering or impossible scene-level overlap patterns.

children.name: Camera Geometry
children.definition: Camera perspective, projection geometry, or viewpoint geometry visible in the figure.

children.name: Physical Plausibility
children.definition: Scene-level physical plausibility such as floating objects, floor contact at scene scale, or impossible arrangements.

children.name: Relation
children.definition: Correctness of relationships between visible entities, parts, attributes, or correspondence points.
children.evaluator_question: Are relationships between visible entities correct?
children.positive_scope: Contact, correspondence, attribute binding, spatial relation, interaction, and part-whole relation.
children.negative_scope: Single-entity pose plausibility, GT/keypoint accuracy, bounding-box accuracy, segmentation quality, and protocol robustness.

children.name: Contact
children.definition: Whether two visible entities or parts touch, connect, intersect, or maintain contact correctly.

children.name: Correspondence
children.definition: Visible correspondence between entities, parts, points, views, or panels.

children.name: Attribute Binding
children.definition: Correct binding of visible attributes to the right entity or part.

children.name: Spatial Relation
children.definition: Pairwise relation such as left/right, above/below, inside/outside, near/far, or in-front/behind.

children.name: Interaction
children.definition: Visible interaction between people, objects, agents, tools, or scene elements.

children.name: Part-Whole Relation
children.definition: Relationship between an object and its visible parts when the relation itself is the criterion.

children.name: Reference Match
children.definition: Fidelity to a visible source, target, ground truth, before-after panel, or comparison reference.
children.evaluator_question: Does the output match a visible source, target, ground truth, or comparison panel?
children.positive_scope: Identity, background, reconstruction, edit preservation, geometry match, style match, mask match, landmark match, and segmentation match.
children.negative_scope: Prompt-only matching, absolute image appearance with no reference, single-object form with no visible reference, and protocol robustness.

children.name: Identity
children.definition: Identity preservation or identity match against a visible source/reference.

children.name: Background
children.definition: Background preservation or match to visible source/reference.

children.name: Reconstruction
children.definition: Reconstruction fidelity against target, source, or ground truth.

children.name: Edit Preservation
children.definition: Preservation of non-edited content in before/after or edit-reference setups.

children.name: Geometry Match
children.definition: Geometric fidelity to visible source, target, annotation, or ground truth.

children.name: Style Match
children.definition: Style fidelity when a visible reference style is the criterion.

children.name: Mask Match
children.definition: Mask fidelity against visible mask, annotation, or ground truth.

children.name: Landmark Match
children.definition: Keypoint, landmark, or pose-coordinate match against visible ground truth or annotation.

children.name: Segmentation Match
children.definition: Segmentation output fidelity against visible ground-truth segmentation.

children.name: Prompt Match
children.definition: Match to a text prompt, caption, instruction, requested content, or requested attribute.
children.evaluator_question: Does the output match the text prompt, caption, or instruction?
children.positive_scope: Object presence, attribute match, spatial instruction, semantic match, text legibility, count match, action match, and expression match.
children.negative_scope: Lighting, expression, physical plausibility, or object quality when not specified by prompt/caption/instruction.

children.name: Object Presence
children.definition: Requested object, entity, category, or scene element is present or absent as specified.

children.name: Attribute Match
children.definition: Requested color, material, style, state, or other attribute is correctly assigned.

children.name: Spatial Instruction
children.definition: Prompt-specified spatial arrangement or relation is satisfied.

children.name: Semantic Match
children.definition: Overall semantic content matches the caption, prompt, or instruction.

children.name: Text Legibility
children.definition: Requested text, glyphs, symbols, or readable writing are rendered correctly.

children.name: Count Match
children.definition: Requested number of objects or entities is correct.

children.name: Action Match
children.definition: Requested action, activity, or event is depicted correctly.

children.name: Expression Match
children.definition: Requested facial expression, emotion, or pose state is depicted correctly.

sidecar.name: Sidecar / Rejected
sidecar.definition: Research concepts that should not be forced into the main qualitative figure tree.

children.name: Temporal Behavior
children.definition: Claims requiring video playback, sequence behavior, flicker, jitter, or temporal dynamics.

children.name: Multi-Sample Diversity
children.definition: Claims requiring multiple generated samples or distribution-level diversity evidence.

children.name: Method Control
children.definition: Claims about controllability or intervention behavior not directly judged from a single qualitative figure.

children.name: Protocol Robustness
children.definition: Claims about robustness to perturbations, occlusion protocols, or test-time conditions.

children.name: Latent Representation
children.definition: Claims about attention maps, internal features, embeddings, or hidden model states when not used as visible figure output.

children.name: Dataset Coverage
children.definition: Claims about dataset distribution, coverage, domain breadth, or benchmark composition.

children.name: Training Memorization
children.definition: Claims about memorization, training data leakage, or learned representations.

children.name: Metric Calibration
children.definition: Claims about numerical metrics, calibration, FID, LPIPS, IoU, or other score behavior.

children.name: Nonvisual Method Property
children.definition: Claims about speed, efficiency, architecture, optimization, or generalization without direct visual figure evidence.
